title: HackerTube: YouTube built from videos recommended by HN
titleZh: HackerTube: YouTube built from videos recommended by HN
author: karpathy
relevanceReason: 命中 3 个 AI/科技关键词。
textRawHtml:
YouTube-style UI over 6,454 videos sourced from 39,834 HN comments since 2007.

https://hackertube.org/
textZhHtml:
YouTube-style UI over 6,454 videos sourced from 39,834 HN comments since 2007.

https://hackertube.org/
summaryRaw: It was Friday night at 11pm, I was tired, I went to YouTube to watch something and realized that I was looking at an enshittified wall of slop. Insanely exaggerated thumbnails, dumb recommendations of the same tired topics, truly terrible idiocracy-grade content. I'm sure this algorithm works well for the median person on the internet, but it definitely does not work for me. So this morning (Saturday) I took a hold of my Opus 5.5 and gave it the task: Let's write our own YouTube clone based on whatever videos have been recommended on Hacker News. And Opus came back with: hackertube.org!

Opus downloaded all comments of HackerNews, filtered them, ran Sonnet over them in a Workflow (Claude Code feature), got rid of spam, and narrowed everything down to 40K comments recommending a YouTube video. In total, we get 6,454 YouTube videos that have been recommended by a few people on HN from 2007-2026 across 150 topics. Then we wrap it up in a YouTube UI, get a domain, push to a VPS, secure, harden, optimize and voila! HackerTube:

Contains quality content Uses the 50% thumbnail instead of the uploaded thumbnail Custom and good ForYou recommendations without any user accounts, storing state in local browser session Keyboard shortcuts Export of the site's data available to give to your agent to easily create your own version

comments.author: theptip
comments.textRawHtml:
I think there is a massive opportunity for this kind of feed disaggregation. Used to be the recommender and indexing of content was hard, now I believe we can likely build our own according to our own preferences.

Haiku/Sonnet (or even Jev) can do a lot of the filtering work to rank and extend an RSS feed list.

I think this gives us an opportunity to fully cut the cord from eyeball merchants who want us to maximally engage and therefore polarize their content.

The big remaining hook will be the social graph; I am interested to see how far the EU push for mandatory interoperability will go. Another angle I’d support would be mandatory pluggable standards for your own ranking algorithm, but it captures less of the win than full disaggregation.

children.author: appplication
children.textRawHtml:
It seems a bit like tragedy of the commons. If we all move towards consuming content this way, who is posting what and where? How is it discovered?

One of the great losses of the age of social media is physical community, as people substitute digital presence for in-person interactions. This is the next step with the loss of digital community.

children.author: numpad0
children.textRawHtml:
Why would those content stop getting made? A lot of hardcore tech YouTubers are university lecturers. Chinese fried rice stalls on TikTok makes living in selling the rice. Japanese anime keeps getting made and aired.

I think there might be a lesson learned from the era of attention economy and also a potential explanation as to what advertiser friendliness was about - the attention economy did not graduate from being a surplus market. Advertisers had no incentives to subsidize the waste byproducts of fried rice stall, but the system was too deeply molded for them. The amount of standalone contents that are native to social media are tiny.

Anyway, I just don't think the contents that are made because of a social feed are the ones that weren't worth much even on social media.

children.author: epiccoleman
children.textRawHtml:
I see the concern, because I agree that social media has to some degree already done this, and that we've lost something in that process.

But - there's no reason this couldn't actually be a good thing. I can totally imagine a platform[0] where the focus is less on creation and more on curation. I sub to some person or community who's going to share good links, and I see only that, instead of the slop firehose from The Algorithm.

(and yes, social media was already more like this, in the early days).

[0] and platform implies more than I mean, could just be some nice wrapper around RSS or activitypub or whatever

children.author: CreepGin
children.textRawHtml:
For me, AI is helping in that respect in weird ways. There are so much AI slop content out there, I find myself doomscrolling much less these days.

And just the other day, I wanted to finally setup a private WoW server for me to play with my wife and kids. We had some random devices around the house: 2 PCs, a Steamdeck, and a MBP. I made sure they were all on the same network. Then, asked Claude Code to set it all up so we can play on the "most stable and latest" client for WoW. We all headed out for tennis. Came back in 2 hours and it was 99% done.

It setup AzerothCore and downloaded Chromiecraft for all 4 devices. It even setup VM Fusion on my mac correctly. I just had to tweak some mouse settings in the end. Normally, all this would take me an entire weekend to do. Pretty crazy how much of the tedious stuff AI can just take care of now.

children.author: diseasedyak
children.textRawHtml:
This is great, bookmarking!

When you say you used Haiku + Jev, how did you work the two together? What part of the process does Jev handle?
children.textZhHtml:

children.author: CreepGin
children.textRawHtml:
Thanks! Haiku is doing the following:

1) tldr summary of each post (when a link is first submitted). 2) Deduping posts. 3) Detecting when there are multiple stories (different links) that are basically covering the same thing, in which case it'll "merge" them by using only the best post (it decides). 4) Come up with titles for posts that don't have them (like twitter/bluesky posts).

Jev is used for:

1) Quickly getting rid of bad posts during the 1st stage of crawling. 2) Determining initial amount of points (based on a scale) awarded to post when it was first submitted.

There are probably few other cases I'm not thinking of right now. But basically, the gist is to use Jev for super frequent classifier tasks that are early in the pipeline so it can save cost.

This will roughly use about $40 of my AI credits per month. Anthropic gives Ultra users $200 monthly credit for API usage. So I'm happy I can make some good use out of it.

children.author: dude187
children.textRawHtml:
I remember finding YouTube videos to watch on the something awful forums in like 2007. Was the only real way I knew of at the time but the variety puts my current recommendation feed to shame.

I miss the sheer random absurdity of what I'd find there. Don't remember too much of what I found any more, other than "man from lox" which I still find someone new to show it to every few years or so lol

I will say the recommendations now being so personalized gives me a lot of big topical chunks of content relevant to my interests that I'd probably not have found on a random SA thread. But so much of it is just "a competing channel of what you're already watching" and "what we are recommending to half the world right now and we can tell you won't object to". Not the random out of thin air things like "ghost ride the whip" (another that just instantly came to my mind lol)

children.author: armchairhacker
children.textRawHtml:
The root problem is not only marketers, but people with “poor taste” i.e. different opinions than yours. You know, like how Redditor’s favorite shows skew towards teenage audiences (superheroes, shonen) because many are teenagers.

A solution to both problems is:

- Filter recommendations to users matching the asker’s personality and other favorites. This works particularly well for bad taste. Marketers can still imitate real users by overwhelming every demographic with accounts that have a small set of genuine recommendations and larger set of hijacked ones, but it requires more accounts.

- Web of trust, letting users explicitly follow others who they know elsewhere and see their followers’ recommendations, and prioritizing for everyone users who are verified real. This does less for taste matching but much more for filtering marketers.
